generated_asset.prompt:
Generate a completely new, high-quality COLOR PHOTOGRAPH for an enterprise website: an authentic candid office scene, landscape 16:9.

Image 1 is THE USER'S THIRD PHOTO and is the SOLE FACIAL IDENTITY REFERENCE. Preserve this woman's face faithfully: its actual facial proportions, eye shape and size, brows, nose, cheek and chin contours, lip shape and expression. Do not blend it with another face, substitute a generic model, reduce or enlarge the eyes, or redesign her features. Match the reference's smooth, even skin appearance and complexion, without inventing additional skin detail. Keep the face natural and photographic, with the same clean skin finish as the reference. No added freckles, spots, acne, scars, roughness, visible grain on the face, beauty-filter exaggeration or illustrated rendering. Faithful facial appearance is the highest priority.

Supporting appearance information from the user's first two photos: her hair is naturally light brown, abundant and curly. Use voluminous loose curls around the face and shoulders, with natural irregular strands and flyaways. This supporting information affects HAIR ONLY, not the facial features established by Image 1. Keep the hair's color restrained and natural, without an orange glow or sculpted glossy ringlets.

Create a fresh scene: she is seated at a wooden table in a contemporary working office, with an open unbranded laptop, in a simple off-white collared shirt. She is listening attentively to a colleague just outside the frame, with her face fully visible in a gentle three-quarter angle close to the reference's facial angle. Her body is relaxed and naturally proportioned, with shoulders at ease, elbows near the table, and hands mostly naturally occluded by the laptop. No raised hand, no tablet, and no hand touching the face. Use a medium environmental shot: the face should be sufficiently large and clearly resolved to retain the reference's recognizable details, while the desk and office remain visibly part of the photograph. Eye-level 50 mm camera perspective with coherent human and furniture scale.

Photographic style: soft window light, gentle warm highlights and understated green-gray office shadows, realistic exposure and restrained contrast, natural wood and glass. Subtle reflections and a softly motion-blurred passing figure at one far edge can echo the website's candid work photography; do not blur or smear the woman's face. Her face is in clear photographic focus, with clean tonal transitions and accurate eyes. Avoid theatrical orange grading, glamour retouching, HDR, artificial glow, plastic rendering, doll-like features or illustration. Keep the expression calm and unposed rather than smiling into the camera.

Composition: landscape 16:9, the woman and her face comfortably inside a central square crop used by the website. Eyes and face lie below the upper quarter, which stays calm for a white heading. Retain a natural head-to-body relationship and enough office context; no enlarged head or elongated torso. The user explicitly wants a new photograph, not a copy of the uploaded photo's composition.

Do not reproduce the reference's black-and-white filter, dark T-shirt, selfie crop, hand gesture or screenshot controls. The back arrow and Edit label are UI and must not appear. No readable text, logos, watermark, frame, duplicate people or extraneous limbs.
generated_asset.export: Selected generated PNG converted to 1600 × 900 WebP with Sharp, quality 92; no generative edits or additional retouching during export.

generated_asset.original_prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: landscape editorial workplace photograph for the Employee assistance card on the Century enterprise website. Output a wide 16:9 photograph that also works cropped to a square.
Inputs: Images 1 and 2 show the woman's appearance; use them for very close visual resemblance with slight natural differences, not as compositions to copy. Images 3 and 4 are the WEBSITE PHOTOGRAPHIC STYLE REFERENCES and must govern this new image's art direction: candid people at work, a stationary subject with people moving around them, cinematic motion blur, restrained warm highlights and deep teal/olive shadows, documentary 35mm photography and fine film grain.
Create a new scene: in a busy office, viewed through a glass partition from several metres away, a woman with very similar facial features to the supplied woman is standing beside a shared worktable, reading a tablet and thoughtfully discussing work with someone just outside the frame. She wears a simple off-white open-collar shirt with sleeves casually rolled. Her light-brown, naturally voluminous curly hair is loosely pulled back with some curls around her face. Show her upper body and surrounding working environment, not a headshot. Her face is in a gentle three-quarter angle, clearly visible but she is not looking into the camera, with a quiet, natural engaged expression. Closely echo the reference woman's soft oval face, eye shape, delicate nose and subtle smile, with modest variations in cheek contour and brow shape so she is a very close lookalike rather than an exact duplicate.
Composition is environmental and cinematic: the woman's head is about 15 percent of the image height, her face is near x=55%, y=45%, her body and desk provide context. Keep her sharp enough to recognize. Place heavily motion-blurred passing colleagues at the FAR left and right edges and soft reflections on the glass; keep her face and the central square crop unobstructed. Quiet darker office architecture and glazing in the top quarter provide space for a white card heading. A laptop, a few papers and normal office furniture are natural contextual details, all unbranded with no readable content.
Match the existing website photos' subdued amber, warm ivory, olive and dark blue-green color palette and filmic contrast. Late-afternoon window light, imperfect real textures, slight underexposure, subtle grain, physically plausible long-exposure motion blur. The image should feel like an observational frame from a sophisticated enterprise documentary, with authentic activity and depth.
Avoid: posed corporate portrait, direct gaze, smile-to-camera, glamour makeup, blazer portrait, centered headshot, bright generic stock-photo office, commercial beauty lighting, pristine AI-smooth skin, exaggerated bokeh, oversaturated colors, logos, readable text, watermarks, typography, graphic overlays, extra sharp faces. No UI and no circular crop.

revisions.edit_prompt:
Edit the existing photograph in Image 1 with TWO PRECISE CORRECTIONS. Image 2 is the user's third photograph, the facial identity and eye-anatomy reference. Image 3 is an existing website photograph and is the color, lighting and motion-blur STYLE reference only.

PRESERVE: the successful facial identity of Image 1, its eye and lip proportions, clear smooth even skin as in Image 2, abundant light-brown curls, naturally proportioned seated body, white shirt, relaxed pose, laptop, office composition and landscape 16:9 framing. Do not replace the woman with a new model, enlarge her eyes, add skin blemishes or turn this into a posed portrait.

CORRECTION 1 — EYES AND HAIR BOUNDARY: carefully repair the eyes and temples so both eyes sit anatomically inside the face, with coherent eyelids, sclera, iris, pupils and surrounding skin. Use Image 2 for faithful eye shape and placement. An eye, iris, pupil or eyelash must never be painted on top of hair or outside the facial contour. Gently move the curls immediately beside both outer eye corners away from the eye region, tucking only those few temple strands back if needed, so the full eyes, eyelids and a narrow natural margin of skin are unobstructed. Keep the overall full curly hairstyle. Keep a plausible, consistent sideways gaze and normal convergence. No doubled outlines, extra lashes, partial extra eyes or hair intersecting an eyeball. Retain the reference woman's facial proportions and appearance.

CORRECTION 2 — WEBSITE PHOTOGRAPHIC STYLE: bring Image 1 close to Image 3's understated cinematic workplace photography. Darker, softly lit office atmosphere; subdued amber and warm-ivory highlights; deep muted teal/olive and graphite shadows; controlled natural contrast and a touch of optical softness in the environment. Reduce the bright generic-office look of the background. Keep gentle directional window light on the woman's face so it remains clear and readable. Strengthen realistic motion blur on the passing figure at the edge and subtle glass reflections in the surrounding office. Blur is only on moving/background elements, NEVER on the woman's eyes, face or hair. Preserve believable photographic color and smooth skin; no orange skin, glow, heavy grain on the face, exaggerated bokeh, beauty-filter rendering or cartoon appearance. Do not borrow the people or their faces from Image 3.

Keep the desk, body, head size and pose coherent and unchanged. Do not add new objects, text, logos, watermark, UI, borders or additional visible faces. The result must be a real-looking candid editorial photograph in the existing site's style, with the user's chosen facial appearance intact and cleanly separated from the curls.
